newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Practical joke, or Taiwan mourning Deng death?.
newsitem.headline: Practical joke, or Taiwan mourning Deng death?.

text.p: A Taiwanese flag at an art museum in central Taichung was altered to look like the red five-star flag of rival communist China, possibly to mourn the late patriarch Deng Xiaoping, news media said on Wednesday.
Another national flag at a Taichung city parking lot also was found to have been sprayed-painted to look like China's, the state-funded Central News Agency said.
Both flew for some time before being found, reports said.

Police said they suspected the flags were altered to honour the passing of Deng, whose February 19 death is being marked on the mainland by six days of official mourning, but could not rule out the possibility of a practical joke.
Beijing held a state funeral on Tuesday for the late leader who introduced market reforms to rejuvenate China's economy and fostered broad though unofficial ties with Taiwan.
In a funeral oration, Deng's heir, President Jiang Zemin, issued his strongest pledge yet to recover the island of Taiwan.
"The Taiwan question will be settled eventually and the complete reunification of the motherland will certainly be achieved," Jiang promised.
Taiwan and China split after Nationalist forces lost a civil war on the mainland in 1949 and withdrew to the offshore island.
Defacing Taiwan's red, white and blue Republic of China flag is considered a national slander and is punishable by up to one year in jail.
Taiwan law does not state clearly whether it is illegal to display the five-star flag of the communist People's Republic.
